findings.evidence: `pkg/ddl/rollingback.go:132` switches on `args.ModifyColumnType` but has no case for legacy `mysql.TypeNull` (6); the default path returns `ErrCancelledDDLJob` without changing `job.State` (so a cancelling job can remain `JobStateCancelling`). Second confirmation: cancel flow in `pkg/ddl/job_worker.go:837-843` calls `convertJob2RollbackJob` for `JobStateCancelling` and sets `updateRawArgs = job.IsRollingback()`; if `rollingbackModifyColumn` leaves state as cancelling, the job is persisted still cancelling and will be retried, potentially wedging the DDL queue. The refactor itself acknowledges legacy `mysql.TypeNull` via normalization in `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:170-178`, but that normalization is not applied in the cancellation/rollback path.
findings.fix: In `rollingbackModifyColumn`, normalize legacy values before the switch: if `args.ModifyColumnType == mysql.TypeNull` (or any unknown/non-enum value), recompute it using the same logic as runtime execution (e.g. `args.ModifyColumnType = getModifyColumnType(args, tblInfo, oldCol, job.SQLMode)`), then proceed so the function always sets `job.State` to `Cancelled` or `Rollingback` deterministically.
findings.impact: Compatibility regression for in-flight or queued modify-column jobs created by older TiDB versions (where `ModifyColumnType` may be `mysql.TypeNull`): `ADMIN CANCEL DDL JOBS` can get stuck with the job remaining in `JobStateCancelling`, repeatedly retried by the worker and potentially blocking subsequent DDL jobs.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master`: `upstream/master:pkg/ddl/rollingback.go` still lacks a `mysql.TypeNull` compatibility branch and still falls through with `return ErrCancelledDDLJob` after the switch; `git log a9bb0133..upstream/master -- pkg/ddl/rollingback.go` shows only refactors/renames and unrelated changes, no compat handling added.
findings.verify: Add a unit test that constructs a `model.Job` in `JobStateCancelling` with `ModifyColumnArgs.ModifyColumnType = mysql.TypeNull` (legacy), then runs the cancel conversion (`convertJob2RollbackJob` / `rollingbackModifyColumn`) and asserts `job.State` becomes `JobStateCancelled` or `JobStateRollingback` (never remains `JobStateCancelling`). Cover both `needChangeColumnData == false` and `== true` shapes (with/without `args.ChangingColumn`).
findings.what: Cancel/rollback path for `ActionModifyColumn` assumes refactored `ModifyColumnType` enum values, but does not handle the legacy `mysql.TypeNull` (6) value used by older jobs, which can leave a job stuck in `JobStateCancelling`.
